answer: Each identity is admitted only after completing a Wesolowski time-lock: a long chain of modular squarings whose next step depends on the previous one. GPUs can run separate chains for cloned identities, but cannot shorten the sequential time required by any one chain, so each Sybil consumes its own physical delay and compute. A cipher-bound challenge at the inlet ties the proof to the current session; an atlas of verified outputs lets peers check results efficiently.
